execution_evidence.reason: Static Rust allocator changes, including the new median-capped policy variants, per-shard fairness test, and matched-trace benchmark remain uncompiled/unexecuted in this environment. The separate NCF-ALLOC-3 Python attack sweep is explicitly research-reference evidence only. Exact-head Rust/TLA+ receipts, real demand traces, and multi-agent/Holochain qualification remain outstanding. NCF-ALLOC-3 source, tests, results, campaign specification, run guide, and limitations documentation are checked in under research/; their execution records identify Python-only evidence separately from the Rust qualification gate. NCF-ALLOC-4 additionally models one fixed 4,000-unit attacker backlog split across 1..32 shard IDs while retaining fifteen honest identities. Five Python tests pass; cryptographic identity, admission economics, Rust and distributed qualification are explicitly not run. A follow-up static audit found that deriving a cap from positive weights when the lower median was zero could let rare positive outliers define their own cap. The median-capped allocator now zeroes the relative weights in that case and triggers the existing equal-share cold-start fallback; mirrored Python/Rust regression definitions were added. Python-only suite now has 10 NCF-ALLOC-3 tests plus 5 NCF-ALLOC-4 tests; Rust still not run. The corpus now also has NCF-ALLOC-022 for sparse positive claims with a zero lower median, requiring the bounded-cap policy to use equal cold-start rights rather than let positive outliers set their own relative cap. NCF-ALLOC-5 adds a sequential obligation-admission oracle, eight Python regressions and a fixed alias-replay result profile. It assumes independently validated verifier evidence and does not imply the verifier is implemented, nor prove concurrent/distributed uniqueness. NCF-ALLOC-5 now binds the immutable accepted record to a canonical obligation-payload digest in addition to principal, instrument and amount; the NCF-ALLOC-027 regression rejects same-ID/same-amount rebindings to different work. This is only downstream admission logic given a verifier result, not a verifier implementation. NCF-ALLOC-5 is now represented by a typed Rust sequential reference module with ten test definitions and an explicit crate-internal verified-evidence trust boundary. NCF-QUAL-007 remains not run. NCF-BENCH-009 defines end-to-end admission/replay/cap-contention performance gates; all throughput targets are aspirational and unmeasured. NCF-ALLOC-6 enumerates 70 interleavings of two four-step admission requests across three scenarios. Eight Python model tests pass locally and the combined NCF-ALLOC-3/4/5/6 test run has 35 passes. The checked-in NCF-ALLOC-6 source is a manually synchronized, bytewise different copy of the local executed script; results are explicitly not checksum-bound CI, and Rust/database/TLC/distributed tests remain not run. NCF-ALLOC-5 now has a typed Rust sequential model with eleven unit-test definitions; the new verifier-evidence-binding regression itself remains uncompiled/unrun. NCF-ALLOC-6 adds finite Python interleaving research with eight locally passed tests, but database/Rust/Holochain concurrency remains unqualified. The Rust obligation constructor missing-field issue was caught by static inspection and fixed by initializing canonical_id_by_payload_digest. The Rust module now has a separate AcceptedObligation verifier-evidence binding per request ID, so aliases can return the original canonical receipt yet still replay consistently against their own first accepted verifier version/digest. A regression is defined for this. The module now declares fourteen test cases; no local Rust compilation is possible here. A new static audit found and fixed a missing canonical_id_by_payload_digest initialization in ObligationBook::new. The Rust accepted record now stores request-ID-specific verifier version/digest separately from the original canonical receipt, so canonical aliases have consistent retry semantics. The Rust module now declares fourteen tests; exact-head build/test/Clippy is still not confirmed. NCF-ALLOC-7 adds a local file-backed SQLite WAL/synchronous-FULL transactional admission baseline. Seven Python tests passed; 150 local concurrent race trials showed zero observed invariant failures and the local 2,000-attempt run measured 1,098.59 attempts/s, p50 1.1528 ms/p95 1.8039 ms/p99 2.1586 ms. These results are single-host SQLite research only. The checked-in source is a condensed, semantically synchronized copy and not byte-identical to the locally executed source. Rust, Holochain/multi-agent, multi-host and production paths remain unqualified. NCF-ALLOC-8 adds six local Python tests, 18 application-process crash injections across six transaction boundaries, and nine synchronized two-process race trials with zero observed invariant failures. A higher-repetition run timed out and is incomplete. Execution used SQLite 3.46.1, so WAL/checkpoint qualification remains blocked pending SQLite 3.51.3 or a verified backport and explicit checkpoint stress; Rust/Holochain/multi-host/power-loss qualification remains not run. NCF-ALLOC-8 follow-up completed a 5x10 campaign with 30 crash injections and 30 process-pair trials, zero observed invariant failures; the terminal tool returned a timeout after the complete artifact was written. NCF-ALLOC-9 added exact-source checkpoint/read stress: 1k, 8k, and two 20k write campaigns, zero recorded invariant failures, plus a held-reader busy-checkpoint regression. Runtime remains SQLite 3.46.1, so the documented WAL-reset engine bug still requires a 3.53.3 (or at minimum 3.51.3/backport) rerun and dedicated low-level qualification. Rust/Holochain/multi-host/power-loss tests remain not run. NCF-ALLOC-9 checkpoint stress now records SQLite sqlite_source_id() and offers --require-fixed-sqlite. On the current 3.46.1 runtime, that guard exits NOT_QUALIFIED as expected. The current official SQLite release observed on 2026-10-28 is 3.54.1; a fixed-engine rerun and special WAL-reset regression still remain open.

claim_ceiling: Reference-model conformance only when executed against a named source revision.
Does not prove Holochain DHT integrity, key custody, real-world service delivery, legal tender status, reserve adequacy, FX parity, or external settlement finality.
Does not prove that production zomes enforce the same properties until separately qualified against exact source and multi-agent runtime evidence.
Lower-median demand caps are bounded-influence heuristics, not demand authentication or Sybil resistance; assumptions about stable shard identity and minority attackers must remain explicit.

Median caps and per-shard equal floors are not Sybil-resistant when one principal can multiply identity slots. NCF-ALLOC-4 is an independent Python identity-splitting model, not an implemented cryptographic identity or admission protocol.
NCF-ALLOC-5 only tests sequential deduplication/principal-cap policy given an externally verified receipt; the verifier flag and deterministic receipt hash are not cryptographic proof.

A canonical obligation-payload digest binds fields only when its input is correctly derived and independently verified; the NCF-ALLOC-5 test model computes the digest locally and does not authenticate underlying work.
The Rust ObligationBook model is sequential and in-memory; it cannot prove concurrent uniqueness, durable idempotency, verifier authenticity, or Holochain cross-agent validation.

A sequential obligation book is not a concurrency proof. NCF-ALLOC-6 is a finite two-client interleaving model; only a tested durable storage transaction or separately proved distributed invariant protocol can qualify concurrent admission.

NCF-ALLOC-6 race counts come from a finite Python scheduler, not real database or distributed concurrency; the Rust obligation module remains sequential and unqualified until exact-head tests and multi-agent evidence exist.
NCF-ALLOC obligation admission Rust tests and constructor fixes remain source-level changes until the dedicated exact-head Rust qualification emits a passing receipt.

NCF-ALLOC-7 results are local file-backed SQLite and local-thread evidence only; they do not establish multi-host durability, actual power-loss safety, cryptographic verification, Rust/Holochain behavior, or production settlement.

NCF-ALLOC-8 demonstrates only bounded application-process crash recovery and independent-process contention on one host using SQLite 3.46.1. It does not simulate kernel crash, power loss, faulty storage, multi-host consensus, Holochain multi-agent validation, cryptographic verification, or production settlement.

SQLite WAL/checkpoint behavior is not qualified by NCF-ALLOC-8 because the local runtime predates the upstream fix for the documented WAL-reset bug; upgrade or verify a backport and run dedicated checkpoint stress before stronger claims.

NCF-ALLOC-9 demonstrates local application-level checkpoint/read/write consistency only on SQLite 3.46.1; it is not a reproducer or certification for SQLite's internal WAL-reset bug, and it does not simulate OS crash or power loss.

NCF-ALLOC-8 follow-up 5x10 result artifact completed (30 crash injections plus 30 independent-process race pairs) despite a terminal timeout response; result completeness and exact v1 source hash were checked separately.

NCF-ALLOC-9 now reports sqlite_source_id() and includes --require-fixed-sqlite. The current SQLite 3.46.1 runtime correctly yields NOT_QUALIFIED against the 3.51.3 minimum. The latest official release observed on 2026-10-28 is SQLite 3.54.1; generic stress remains distinct from the dedicated WAL-reset regression.

invariants.name: Instrument identity is not ticker identity
invariants.statement: Distinct canonical instrument IDs remain distinct even when symbol, display name, or numeric amount is identical.

invariants.name: Canonical profile binding
invariants.statement: Authorization and value mutations resolve instrument properties from a canonical registry; a caller cannot supply an alternate profile at the operation boundary.

invariants.name: Action-scoped authority
invariants.statement: A capability is valid only for its exact issuer, delegate, instrument, action, current revision, expiry, and declared amount ceiling.

invariants.name: Mutual-credit conservation
invariants.statement: Each accepted mutual-credit event changes provider and receiver positions by equal and opposite amounts within that instrument.

invariants.name: Atomic rejection
invariants.statement: A rejected event changes neither balances, outstanding obligations, nor consumed event IDs.

invariants.name: Idempotent replay
invariants.statement: An exact retry has one effect; reusing an event ID with a different payload is rejected.

invariants.name: Bounded federation exposure
invariants.statement: Outstanding obligations remain within each peering-edge cap and any configured aggregate gross-exposure cap scoped to that exact instrument; raw amounts from unlike instruments are never summed.

invariants.name: Risk stop with safe unwind
invariants.statement: Pausing new obligations blocks new exposure while allowing separately authorized settlement of already-incurred obligations.

invariants.name: Denomination stability
invariants.statement: An instrument ID cannot silently change its denomination identity or scale; migration requires a new instrument identity or an explicit qualified migration.

invariants.name: Same-revision profile consistency
invariants.statement: A profile's policy fields cannot change without a revision change; revisioned updates must preserve immutable issuer, family, and denomination semantics.

invariants.name: Aggregate exposure is instrument-scoped
invariants.statement: Aggregate gross exposure compares amounts only within the same canonical instrument/unit domain; unlike currencies require a separately qualified conversion/risk model before risk-value aggregation.

invariants.name: Gross obligations do not implicitly net
invariants.statement: Opposing directional obligations remain separately outstanding by default. Signed net position is diagnostic only and may not substitute for gross exposure limits; settlement must identify the direction being reduced. Netting requires a separately qualified agreement and enforcement path.

invariants.name: Clearing agreements bind a canonical instrument profile
invariants.statement: A clearing agreement can be created only for a registered instrument and pins the exact profile revision. Unknown IDs and stale profile revisions fail closed; non-transferable reputation-family instruments cannot be used as spendable clearing instruments.

invariants.name: Partitioned exposure rights are preallocated and non-overlapping
invariants.statement: During disconnected operation, each shard may consume only its previously allocated reservation. Reservation slices across shards, agreements and epochs are counted against the exact community/instrument cap; prior-epoch slices are not reclaimed without coordinated fencing/reconciliation.

invariants.name: Reservation agreement identity binds counterparties
invariants.statement: A reservation agreement ID identifies one immutable community pair across instruments, shards, and epochs. Budget slices cannot be reassigned to a different counterparty pair by reusing the agreement identifier.

invariants.name: Fence precedes transfer
invariants.statement: A successor allocation cannot become spendable until the prior epoch has a verifiable fencing decision in the authoritative control chain.

invariants.name: One active owner per allocation epoch
invariants.statement: Every spendable allocation has exactly one owner under the verified control chain; old and successor epochs cannot both create accepted exposure against the same rights.

invariants.name: No timeout-only reallocation
invariants.statement: A timeout, missed heartbeat or local clock comparison alone cannot reclaim risk rights from a potentially live owner.

invariants.name: Complete reconciliation before transfer
invariants.statement: If the accepted operation set through the terminal cut or pending exposure is unresolved, transferable capacity is unknown and no transfer may succeed.

invariants.name: Risk-right transfer is conserved
invariants.statement: A transferred unit is debited from the old allocation and credited to at most one successor allocation in a recoverable control-plane transition.

invariants.name: Receipts are canonical and payload-bound
invariants.statement: Receipts bind scope, instrument/profile, caps/policy revisions, owner, epoch, predecessor and payload digest; exact retries are idempotent and conflicting reuse fails closed.

invariants.name: Stale policy revisions cannot transfer rights
invariants.statement: Instrument, community-cap or agreement-cap revision mismatch blocks transfer unless an explicit authorized migration is qualified.

invariants.name: Crash recovery preserves last verified state
invariants.statement: Recovery after any failed transition does not create duplicated spendable capacity or advance beyond the last verified committed control receipt.

invariants.name: Ledger and control operations share one idempotency namespace
invariants.statement: A monetary event ID cannot alias a drain, fencing, or transfer receipt ID; every transition ID is globally unique within the allocation reference model and payload-bound.

invariants.name: Aggregate reservation rights are non-overlapping across shards
invariants.statement: For each exact capacity/instrument domain, the sum of shard reservations never exceeds the configured aggregate budget; every shard's outstanding exposure remains within its own allocated slice, including during partitioned operation.

invariants.name: Shard allocation rights are frozen during a partition
invariants.statement: After a partition begins, the reserved-capacity vector for the affected budget domain remains unchanged until the partition heals or an explicitly coordinated fencing/reconciliation protocol authorizes reallocation.

invariants.name: Lost-response retry preserves the original economic effect
invariants.statement: After a transfer is durably committed but its response is lost, retrying the same canonical transfer ID and payload returns the original receipt and creates no additional capacity or commit.

invariants.name: Conflicting idempotency payloads are rejected
invariants.statement: Reusing a committed transfer ID with any changed canonical payload is rejected, returns no success receipt, and produces no economic mutation.

invariants.name: Replay protection outlives the declared offline horizon
invariants.statement: A committed operation ID or replay-prevention tombstone is retained until every protocol-defined stale-owner and offline-replay condition has been closed. If the safe replay horizon is unknown, the ID is not recycled.

invariants.name: Static allocation conserves the risk budget
invariants.statement: Contingency reserve plus the sum of all static shard rights equals the total configured capacity, with no overflow or overspend.

invariants.name: Static allocation is canonical and deterministic
invariants.statement: The same canonical shard demands, minima, policy parameters, capacity and seed-independent input produce identical per-shard rights regardless of input order; deterministic tie breaks use stable shard IDs.

invariants.name: Forecast signals never authorize partition-time reallocation
invariants.statement: Historical demand samples affect only the pre-partition allocation plan. The allocator cannot mutate active rights or reclaim an unreachable owner's reservation.

invariants.name: Missing demand history is not interpreted as zero demand
invariants.statement: A demand-dependent allocation policy rejects incomplete per-shard history unless an explicit cold-start/fairness rule is configured; a new or unobserved shard is not silently assigned zero weight.

invariants.name: An allocation plan is bound to one canonical instrument
invariants.statement: All shard demand samples and returned rights in a plan share one exact canonical instrument ID; mixed-instrument inputs are rejected and no display ticker substitutes for identity.

invariants.name: Equal-floor weighting redistributes only pre-partition discretionary rights
invariants.statement: An equal-floor demand policy apportions its declared floor equally and its remainder by the declared demand weights, while conserving the same instrument budget and never mutating active reservations.

invariants.name: Admission identity and cap transition is atomic
invariants.statement: Canonical-work uniqueness, request-ID payload binding, principal/instrument cap check and debit, accepted-obligation persistence, and replay response state share one durable serialization point or a separately qualified invariant-confluent protocol.

invariants.name: Accepted liability counters equal accepted obligations
invariants.statement: No concurrent stale-read or snapshot-overwrite path can make the stored used-capacity counter diverge from the sum of accepted outstanding obligations.

invariants.name: Obligation ID binds verifier evidence
invariants.statement: Exact request-ID retries must match the accepted canonical work, principal, instrument, amount, verifier version and verifier-receipt digest; shard, epoch and local sequence may vary only according to the declared retry contract. Conflicts cannot mutate the original receipt or exposure.

invariants.name: Admission and receipt persistence share a durable transaction
invariants.statement: For a qualified storage implementation, cap check/debit, canonical-work uniqueness, request-ID payload/evidence binding, accepted obligation record and replay receipt must commit atomically or be implemented by a separately proven invariant-confluent protocol.

invariants.name: SQLite reference tests do not imply distributed uniqueness
invariants.statement: Local file-backed database transaction results do not qualify multi-host writes, Holochain DHT uniqueness, cryptographic work verification, or production settlement; these require separate exact-source, multi-agent and fault-injection evidence.

invariants.name: Admission crash atomicity
invariants.statement: After application-process termination before the durable commit, recovery exposes none of the obligation, request binding, cap debit, or receipt; after commit, recovery exposes the complete accepted state and exact retry cannot debit again.

invariants.name: Recovered liability ledger consistency
invariants.statement: After restart/recovery, stored used units equal the sum of unique canonical outstanding obligations and remain within the configured principal/instrument cap.

invariants.name: Snapshot ledger coherence during checkpoint concurrency
invariants.statement: The liability counter and aggregate obligation sum read within the same database transaction describe one consistent committed snapshot, even while writers and checkpoints run concurrently.

invariants.name: Checkpoint progress is not admission success or corruption
invariants.statement: A busy or partial checkpoint is recorded as a storage-progress outcome and does not by itself imply acceptance/rejection or data corruption; ledger invariants are checked independently and again after quiescence.

invariants.name: Quiescent checkpoint restores an explicit clean boundary
invariants.statement: After concurrent writers and readers stop, the final checkpoint must complete and reopened state must reconcile used units with unique accepted obligations, preserve key uniqueness, and pass SQLite integrity/foreign-key checks.

conformance_cases.title: Bounded capability accepts an in-limit action
Capability cannot be used by a different actor or for an ungranted action
conformance_cases.attack: Impersonate the named delegate or reuse a capability for another action.

conformance_cases.title: Amount ceiling fails closed when amount is missing
conformance_cases.attack: Call a mutation with a bounded capability but omit the amount.

conformance_cases.title: Negative amount cannot bypass a ceiling
conformance_cases.attack: Submit a negative amount where a bounded operation is expected.

conformance_cases.title: Unbounded issuance capability is rejected
conformance_cases.attack: Attempt issuance without a declared maximum amount.

conformance_cases.title: Inactive instrument rejects new issuance
conformance_cases.attack: Issue while instrument is inactive, using a capability matching the registered issuer and revision.

conformance_cases.title: Paused or inactive instrument can permit separately authorized settlement
Duplicate ticker does not alias distinct instruments
conformance_cases.attack: Register two distinct instrument IDs with the same display symbol.

conformance_cases.title: Reusing an instrument ID with another issuer is rejected
conformance_cases.attack: Register an existing canonical instrument ID under an attacker-controlled issuer.

conformance_cases.title: Mutual-credit event conserves net position
Stale profile revision cannot authorize a new mutation
conformance_cases.attack: Submit an event created for revision N to a registry that contains revision N+1.

conformance_cases.title: Wrong instrument family cannot use mutual-credit operations
conformance_cases.attack: Use a resource-credit profile in the mutual-credit exchange API.

conformance_cases.title: Balance limit rejection is atomic
conformance_cases.attack: Submit an exchange that would exceed a participant balance limit.

conformance_cases.title: Same event ID and same payload is idempotent
conformance_cases.attack: Retry an already accepted event without changing its payload.

conformance_cases.title: Same event ID with changed payload is rejected
conformance_cases.attack: Reuse an accepted exchange ID with a changed amount.

conformance_cases.title: Per-edge exposure limit is enforced
conformance_cases.attack: Increase one peering obligation beyond its bilateral cap.

conformance_cases.title: Aggregate gross exposure across edges is enforced
conformance_cases.attack: Commit exposure on one federation edge, then overcommit aggregate capacity through another edge.

conformance_cases.title: Rejected over-cap event ID is not consumed
conformance_cases.attack: Retry the same event ID with a valid in-cap amount after an over-cap attempt is rejected.

conformance_cases.title: Stale agreement revision is rejected
conformance_cases.attack: Post an obligation using a revision other than the registered agreement revision.

conformance_cases.title: Pause blocks new obligations but permits existing settlement
Settlement cannot exceed outstanding obligation
conformance_cases.attack: Settle a value greater than the remaining signed obligation.

conformance_cases.title: Settlement retry is idempotent and payload-bound
conformance_cases.attack: Retry a settlement ID once with the same payload and once with a changed amount.

conformance_cases.title: Same instrument ID cannot silently change unit or scale
conformance_cases.attack: Present a same-ID, same-revision profile with changed denomination semantics after balances exist.

conformance_cases.title: Same-revision credit-limit widening is rejected
conformance_cases.attack: Present a registry profile with the same instrument ID and revision but a more permissive balance limit after a previous operation.

conformance_cases.title: Revisioned policy update preserves instrument identity and denomination
Aggregate exposure does not sum raw amounts across unlike instruments
conformance_cases.attack: Open an obligation in another instrument while a same-instrument peer-edge cap is nearly or fully used.

conformance_cases.title: New obligations require explicit aggregate caps for both communities
conformance_cases.attack: Attempt a new obligation when either involved community has not configured an aggregate cap for the exact instrument.

conformance_cases.title: A zero aggregate cap explicitly blocks new exposure
conformance_cases.attack: Attempt a new obligation when one community has explicitly set the exact instrument's aggregate cap to zero.

conformance_cases.title: Rejected missing-cap and zero-cap attempts do not consume event identity
conformance_cases.attack: Retry the identical event ID after both communities install a positive, adequate cap; it must apply once, not be stuck as a phantom prior event.

conformance_cases.title: Opposing obligations do not silently net against gross-exposure caps
conformance_cases.attack: Record an obligation from A to B followed by a reverse obligation from B to A; risk checks must use the sum of both unsettled directions, not the signed net.

conformance_cases.title: Clearing agreement cannot reference an unregistered instrument
conformance_cases.attack: Attempt to create a peer clearing agreement for an instrument ID absent from the canonical registry.

conformance_cases.title: Clearing agreement must pin the current instrument profile revision
conformance_cases.attack: Create an agreement whose instrument_revision differs from the canonical registry's profile revision.

conformance_cases.title: Non-transferable reputation cannot be used as a spendable clearing instrument
conformance_cases.attack: Attempt to bind a reputation-family instrument such as MYCEL to a clearing agreement.

conformance_cases.title: Settlement reduces only the explicitly selected obligation direction
conformance_cases.attack: Create outstanding obligations in both directions and submit a settlement for only one direction; verify the opposite direction remains outstanding.

conformance_cases.title: Settlement event identity is bound to direction
conformance_cases.attack: Reuse a settlement ID with the same amount and agreement but the opposite direction; the retry must reject instead of settling a different obligation leg.

conformance_cases.title: Partitioned shards cannot exceed their pre-allocated gross-risk slices
conformance_cases.attack: Two disconnected writers attempt to consume more than their disjoint reservations collectively permit.

conformance_cases.title: Reservation allocation requires explicit community and agreement caps
conformance_cases.attack: Attempt to reserve capacity before either involved community or the agreement has a configured cap.

conformance_cases.title: Settlement restores reusable capacity only within its own reservation
conformance_cases.attack: Settle 40 units on shard A, then attempt to use 61 units on shard B whose reservation is 60; only A's own reservation may reuse the released 40.

conformance_cases.title: Reservation caps are not summed across unlike instrument units
conformance_cases.attack: Allocate separate hour and water units for the same communities and verify that each exact instrument has its own cap.

conformance_cases.title: Old-epoch reservation remains charged until explicit coordinated rebalancing
conformance_cases.attack: Try to allocate the same capacity to a new epoch while the old reservation has not been retired/fenced.

conformance_cases.title: Explicit zero community or agreement cap prevents reservations
conformance_cases.attack: Attempt to allocate a positive shard reservation when either community cap or the agreement cap is zero.

conformance_cases.title: Event ID cannot be replayed against another shard reservation
conformance_cases.attack: Reuse an accepted event ID with a different reservation key/shard; the conflicting replay must reject with no second obligation.

conformance_cases.title: Reservation slices preserve one immutable counterparty pair per agreement ID
conformance_cases.attack: Try to reserve another shard or instrument under an existing agreement ID but substitute one community; the shared identifier must not silently represent a different bilateral agreement.

benchmark_campaigns.name: Mutual-credit conservation, throughput, and idempotency stress
benchmark_campaigns.target: 0 net-position drift and exactly one state effect per unique event
benchmark_campaigns.methodology: Run the exact-head wrapper on a clean checkout. Keep the JSON output and receipt SHA-256. Repeat with multiple recorded seeds and matched hardware/toolchains before comparative claims.

benchmark_campaigns.name: Federation scale and partition behavior
benchmark_campaigns.reservation_reference_harness_claim_ceil: Single-process deterministic reservation-model benchmark only; does not measure network partitions, true concurrent writers, Holochain/DHT, external settlement or distributed fencing.
benchmark_campaigns.reservation_reference_harness_methodolog: Run the clean-checkout wrapper at the exact committed revision with 2+ shards, several fixed seeds, matched toolchain/hardware, and retain the JSON plus binary/output receipt digests. Compare utilization and latency alongside cap-rejection correctness; do not treat unused reserved capacity as free capacity.

benchmark_campaigns.name: Comparative institutional welfare and risk vector
benchmark_campaigns.method: Matched workload and shock traces, fixed and held-out shocks, multiple recorded seeds, ablations, and independent recomputation. Do not collapse metrics into one score.

benchmark_campaigns.name: Partitioned-risk fencing state-machine model checking
benchmark_campaigns.claim_ceiling: A deterministic state-machine/model-checker result only for the declared authority and fault model. It does not prove production Holochain behavior, legal settlement, cryptographic key security or safety outside the explored model.
benchmark_campaigns.methodology: Run the bounded NCF-FEN safe lifecycle model and the NCF-ESCROW two-shard safe model at Capacity=2 and four operation steps; require both to complete without invariant violations. The escrow model freezes its reservation vector during a partition. Then require four unsafe mutants to be detected specifically: timeout-only reallocation -> NoTransferWithoutFence; stale-owner write after transfer -> NoOldWriteOutsideActive; duplicate full-budget allocation across shards -> ReservedCapacityBound; resizing a shard's reservation during a partition -> PartitionedReservationsStayFixed. Parser/tool failures do not count as detection. These results are not yet confirmed. Then qualify the independent transition oracle and exhaust small interleavings. Extend with at least 10,000 reproducible schedules for retries, duplicate/reordered/dropped receipts, stale-owner writes, crashes and partition/heal traces. Keep honest-crash and adversarial-owner campaigns separate. Compare static-quota, acknowledged-drain and any linearizable/quorum mode under identical traces. Any safety violation fails the campaign; utilization and latency are reported only alongside correctness results. The fail-closed runner requires a clean checkout and caller-supplied TLA2TOOLS_JAR; it records source/model/config/JAR hashes and raw logs outside the repository.
benchmark_campaigns.workflow_claim_ceiling: The dedicated draft-PR workflow checks two finite TLA+ models and sensitivity to four deliberately unsafe mutants only; it does not qualify the Rust implementation, distributed concurrency, Holochain validators, or 10,000-schedule model checking.

benchmark_campaigns.name: Safety-qualified liquidity and capacity-utilization frontier
benchmark_campaigns.methodology: Run the exact same deterministic demand/fault traces against each implemented policy and matched hardware/toolchains. Report results only after hard safety gates pass. Plot a Pareto frontier across economic demand served, safely reclaimable versus stranded capacity, tail latency, and compute cost; do not collapse outcomes into a single weighted score. Separate unreachable-owner partitions from honest crash/restart and byzantine-owner campaigns. Include ablations for priority classes and rebalancing policy. Add a low-risk paradigm-shift baseline: optimize the placement of already-authorized, non-overlapping slices before the partition, using training demand traces and robust quantiles. Evaluate on held-out and shifted workloads, and never allow the forecast to enlarge/reassign rights during the partition. This isolates safe capacity-placement improvements from risky online reclamation. An executable dependency-free Rust allocator and benchmark were added. It uses checked integer arithmetic, stable shard-ID tie-breaking, and largest-remainder apportionment; the benchmark compares six policies on the same generated stationary and shifted trace sets. Its current generator is synthetic and single-process. Run the exact-head wrapper, then replace/augment synthetic traces with independently sourced demand profiles before making real-world claims. The executable simulator includes 25%, 50%, and 75% equal-floor variants, creating a small safety-preserving frontier between historical utilization and resilience to demand-shape changes. These variants affect only the initial static placement and cannot resize allocations in a partition. Per-shard demand-served and worst-shard service are reported alongside aggregate utilization; do not treat high overall service as fair if the least-served shard is materially worse. A dedicated adversarial unit test checks that worst-shard and per-shard service metrics expose an underserved shard that aggregate demand-served percentage alone would hide. The matched-trace benchmark now includes two lower-median-capped equal-floor variants (2x and 4x) alongside the original six, yielding sixteen policy/mode reports. These caps limit extreme historical mean weights only under a stable identity set and a minority-attacker assumption; they are not demand authentication or Sybil resistance. The separate NCF-BENCH-006 research campaign compares these trade-offs under inflated claims.
benchmark_campaigns.claim_ceiling: Current executable: deterministic synthetic single-process allocation simulation with integer budget checks only. It does not emit distributed tail latency, partition recovery, economic-demand classes or network measures. Those are requirements for a future multi-agent implementation benchmark. No runtime result is claimed until exact-head Rust tests/benchmark and receipt succeed. Median caps are experimental bounded-influence heuristics only; they do not authenticate queues, prevent cheap Sybil creation, or represent evidence of adversarial distributed safety.

reservation_policy_experiment.hypothesis: Demand-aware allocation of non-overlapping rights before a partition can improve economic demand served without relaxing partition safety or requiring any partition-time reallocation.
reservation_policy_experiment.evaluation: Train allocation weights only on recorded training traces; evaluate on held-out and distribution-shift traces. Report per-shard unserved demand, safe capacity usage, fragmented/unused quota, forecast error, and essential-service demand served. Any safety violation disqualifies the policy regardless of utilization.
reservation_policy_experiment.claim_boundary: An optimization of pre-authorized quota placement, not a method for safely reclaiming an unreachable owner's active rights.

benchmark_campaigns.name: Bounded-influence demand claims and honest-hotspot trade-off

topology.partition_model: none in this campaign; partition semantics remain covered by NCF-BENCH-005 / NCF-FEN

benchmark_campaigns.methodology: Generate the same true-backlog cases for raw weights, 2x and 4x lower-median caps, and the idealized true-backlog oracle. In adversarial cases, 1 to 4 of 16 shards inflate reports by 2x to 20x without increasing actual backlog. Keep IDs stable, state explicitly that there is no Sybil creation, and evaluate honest 4x hotspot service separately. Preserve the multi-dimensional frontier; do not choose a cap from aggregate throughput alone. A Rust version must later reproduce exact integer allocations / claims where the workload is identical before this campaign can be called Rust-qualified.
benchmark_campaigns.claim_ceiling: 20,000-case independent Python research sweep only. No Rust build/test, model-checking, distributed protocol or production result is claimed. Lower-median caps do not authenticate demand and do not resist a Sybil majority or identity churn.

benchmark_campaigns.name: Identity splitting and Sybil influence on bounded allocation
benchmark_campaigns.methodology: Hold the attacker's underlying true backlog at 4,000 units and keep fifteen honest identities at 4,000 units each. Divide the same attacker's fixed workload among increasing numbers of shard IDs, inflate each split claim by 20x, and compare raw weighting, equal-floor, median-capped and true-backlog-oracle policies under the same spendable budget. Retain each case; do not report an averaged score that hides the identity-multiplication boundary. At least one case must show the median cap becoming ineffective. The model does not implement cryptographic identity or admission controls.
benchmark_campaigns.claim_ceiling: Deterministic Python allocation model only. It models one fixed backlog split over multiple IDs, but not cryptographic identity, identity issuance costs, governance, Holochain, distributed concurrency or production settlement. Median caps are not a Sybil defence.

benchmark_campaigns.name: Canonical obligation deduplication and principal-scoped admission

topology.model: sequential reference model; verifier is assumed external

benchmark_campaigns.methodology: Hold one accepted obligation and its principal/instrument/amount fixed, then replay it through increasing shard aliases and epochs. Change exactly one immutable payload field per negative case and require rejection with no change to the accepted ledger projection. Aggregate caps over distinct obligation IDs for the same canonical principal/instrument, independent of shard. The model assumes the verifier receipt was independently authenticated and accepted; verifier cryptography and concurrent/distributed uniqueness remain out of scope. The immutable accepted payload includes a canonical obligation-payload digest, so reusing an ID for different underlying content must conflict even if principal/instrument/amount fields are held constant. The Python model's digest is deterministic test data, not external proof of actual work. The typed Rust reference module additionally treats a retry with the same obligation ID but different verifier version or verifier-receipt digest as a conflict; exact shard/epoch/sequence variation remains allowed and returns the original receipt.
benchmark_campaigns.claim_ceiling: Sequential Python model only. A deterministic digest is not a signature; verifier_receipt_ok is a trusted input. Does not prove cryptographic identity, real-work truth, concurrent uniqueness, Holochain validation or production settlement.

benchmark_campaigns.name: End-to-end obligation admission throughput, replay pressure and principal-cap contention
benchmark_campaigns.methodology: Measure the full admission path rather than the allocator formula. Start with the sequential reference model as a semantic oracle, then compare a durable idempotency store and the real Holochain/multi-agent authority path using the same generated operation histories. Inject retries, crashes, dropped acknowledgements, concurrent same-ID submissions and partitions. Do not compare headline TPS unless identical finality, retry semantics, durability, hardware and transaction steps are declared.

targets.initial_after_safety_qualification: 1000 accepted local obligations/s for 30 minutes on a declared 16-shard testbed, p99 local admission under 100 ms
targets.stretch_not_achieved: 6000 end-to-end settlements/s for a declared 12-step path under matched semantics
targets.long_term_research_only: 10000 TPS investigation; not a claim of parity with BIS proof of concept

benchmark_campaigns.claim_ceiling: This campaign defines measurements only; no throughput, tail latency, durability, distributed correctness or production outcome is claimed.

benchmark_campaigns.name: Concurrent obligation admission race frontier

topology.model: finite Python interleaving model; not real threads

benchmark_campaigns.methodology: Enumerate all 70 order-preserving interleavings of two clients executing read_dedup, read_used, check and commit. Compare two vulnerable check-then-commit counter models with a serializable reference oracle. Use exact histories across the naive and oracle models; require each vulnerability negative control to be reproduced before treating the oracle as meaningful. Later run the same histories against a real durable transaction and multi-agent authority path.
benchmark_campaigns.claim_ceiling: Finite synthetic scheduler only. No threads, storage durability, real database, Holochain or production code is tested.

research_reference.note: Local source/test hashes differ from checked-in copy hashes; local results are research evidence, not a checksum-bound CI artifact.

benchmark_campaigns.name: Durable local SQLite admission baseline under concurrent requests
benchmark_campaigns.methodology: Run actual local SQLite connections from two Python threads. Use file-backed WAL, synchronous FULL and BEGIN IMMEDIATE so canonical-work dedup lookup, request-ID payload binding, cap check/debit, accepted canonical record, verifier-evidence binding and receipt persistence share one write transaction. Execute 50 paired trials for each of three races: distinct 60-unit work against cap 100, same work under different request IDs, and same request ID with conflicting payloads. Also restart the book object after commit to simulate a lost response and retry. Run a 2,000-attempt local mix of 1,000 unique obligations and 1,000 exact replays; report tail latency and throughput without comparing directly to network settlement TPS.
benchmark_campaigns.claim_ceiling: Local file-backed SQLite and local threads only. Checked-in code and local source are bytewise different and not a checksum-bound CI artifact. Does not qualify multi-host storage, actual power-loss behavior, cryptographic verification, Rust, Holochain or Mycelix production safety.

research_reference.note: The checked-in source is condensed and not byte-identical to the locally executed source; results are local research, not exact-source CI evidence.

benchmark_campaigns.name: Crash-boundary recovery and independent-process admission

topology.crash_model: os._exit in child process; application-process death only

benchmark_campaigns.methodology: Run three repetitions at each of six crash boundaries and three synchronized independent-process race cases. Reopen the file after every child-process exit, validate canonical-work/request/cap/receipt consistency, then retry by idempotency key. A follow-up 5 x 10 repetition campaign completed in 45.6385 seconds: 30 crash injections and 30 independent-process pair trials, zero observed invariant failures. The terminal invocation returned a timeout although the complete result artifact existed and its source SHA was verified. Before stronger WAL claims, repeat on SQLite 3.51.3 or later (or a verified backport) and add concurrent checkpoint/reopen stress.
benchmark_campaigns.claim_ceiling: Application-process crash recovery and independent-process contention on one local host only. Runtime was SQLite 3.46.1, older than the upstream fix for the documented WAL-reset bug; checkpoint/power-loss behavior is not qualified.

research_reference.note: The checked-in result JSON is a normalized transcription of the locally generated result; the source itself is verified bytewise against the locally executed file. The high-repetition run timed out and is incomplete.

benchmark_campaigns.engine_gate: Runtime SQLite 3.46.1 is within the version range described by SQLite's WAL-reset bug documentation. Repeat on SQLite 3.53.3, or at minimum 3.51.3 / a verified vendor backport; generic stress is not the low-level bug reproducer.

benchmark_campaigns.name: SQLite WAL checkpoint concurrency and ledger-consistency stress
baselines: no-checkpoint concurrent writer baseline (future matched run)
workloads: 1,000 writes with 750 checkpoint attempts and 900 snapshots
8,000 writes with 2,500 checkpoint attempts and 4,000 snapshots
20,000 writes with 5,000 checkpoint attempts and 6,000 snapshots, repeated twice
quiescent final checkpoint and reopened ledger reconciliation
benchmark_campaigns.methodology: Run four campaigns against the same exact local source: 1k, 8k, and two 20k runs. A barrier starts writer/checkpointer/readers together. Each writer commits one obligation per BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction; readers query counter and obligation aggregate within one read transaction; the checkpointer cycles PASSIVE/RESTART/TRUNCATE and logs busy/partial separately. A dedicated test holds a reader snapshot to force a busy TRUNCATE checkpoint, then releases it and requires a final [0,0,0] checkpoint. This is not SQLite's low-level WAL-reset bug reproducer. The harness captures sqlite_source_id() and has --require-fixed-sqlite, which exits NOT_QUALIFIED on runtimes below 3.51.3. The current 3.46.1 runtime correctly fails this gate.
benchmark_campaigns.claim_ceiling: Single-host application-level SQLite stress only on runtime 3.46.1, which fails the fixed-runtime gate. Not low-level WAL-reset bug reproduction, power-loss/storage-fault qualification, or distributed/production evidence.

qualification_campaigns.name: Exact-head Rust reference-model qualification
qualification_campaigns.method: Run format, tests, and clippy independently; continue after a failed check so the receipt captures all three outcomes. Require the overall result to pass only when all checks pass. Checkout is exact-head, the worktree must be clean, CARGO_TARGET_DIR and logs live outside the checkout, and the receipt binds the source commit/tree, manifest/lock/source digests, compiler identity and per-check log digests. The receipt explicitly includes allocation and obligation module digests alongside the source-tree SHA, so the exact policy/admission modules are named in the evidence artifact.
qualification_campaigns.claim_ceiling: Formatting, tests and clippy for the exact standalone Rust reference crate only. Does not establish distributed/Holochain safety, cryptographic fencing, external settlement finality or production ledger correctness.

qualification_campaigns.name: Deterministic generated fencing lifecycle sweep
invariants_checked: new exposure is rejected after drain/fence
failed transfer and spend attempts do not consume idempotency identity
transferred slice does not exceed verified free capacity
old outstanding + unresolved pending + successor outstanding never exceeds aggregate capacity
successor outstanding never exceeds successor reservation
qualification_campaigns.method: A dependency-free deterministic LCG selects small capacities, initial gross exposure, settlements before/during drain, exposure extensions, pending exposure, and successor spend amounts. qualification_campaigns.claim_ceiling: Unit tests plus synthetic single-process matched-trace evaluation only; real-demand validity and distributed/Holochain safety remain separate. Median caps are not proof of demand or Sybil resistance; the independent Python research sweep is not a Rust or distributed qualification result. When the lower median is zero, the median-capped policy uses equal cold-start allocation rather than deriving a cap from positive outliers alone; this is a defined policy fallback, not a claim that sparse demand is equal in reality. Zero-lower-median capped policy falls back to equal-share cold-start; a positive outlier must not define its own cap.

qualification_campaigns.name: Concurrent admission interleaving model
qualification_campaigns.acceptance: Eight local Python model tests pass, enumerating 70 interleavings per case. Naive negative controls reproduce duplicated canonical work, cap overshoot, conflicting same-ID payloads, and liability counter undercount. The serializable oracle has zero violations in both transaction orders. The result does not qualify real concurrent storage semantics.

qualification_campaigns.name: Local SQLite durable-admission reference baseline
qualification_campaigns.acceptance: Seven local Python tests passed. Fifty trials per each of three concurrent request pairs showed zero local invariant failures; 2,000 sequential attempts produced 1,000 unique accepts and 1,000 exact replays at 1,098.59 attempts/s, p50 1.1528 ms, p95 1.8039 ms and p99 2.1586 ms. All results are single-host SQLite only and are not comparable to networked settlement throughput. Repository source differs bytewise from execution source.

qualification_campaigns.name: Crash-boundary and independent-process admission reference qualification
qualification_campaigns.acceptance: Six local Python tests pass for the resource-safe v2 harness with ResourceWarning promoted to error. The initial campaign ran 18 crash injections plus nine independent-process pair trials; a repeat campaign ran 30 crash injections plus 30 process-pair trials, zero observed invariant failures, in 45.6385 seconds. The complete repeat artifact and exact v1 source SHA were checked despite the terminal tool returning a timeout. This is application-process crash evidence on one host only. SQLite 3.46.1 predates the documented WAL-reset fix; repeat on SQLite 3.53.3 or at minimum 3.51.3 / a verified backport and qualify checkpoints separately.
